clue.text: Malignant, one's left with time inside — unlike Archer

indicators.note: the time word is put within what remains of the malignant word
one's left reads as one has left, so a single I departs from the word for malignant

parts.note: malignant and vicious both mean full of ill will
the Roman numeral for one
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A jab at Jeffrey Archer: someone malicious, but at least honest, unlike the novelist jailed for lying.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeffrey Archer, Tory peer and novelist, was jailed in 2001 for perjury, so the opposite of him is truthful.
explanation.definitionFit: Veracious means habitually truthful, the quality a convicted perjurer conspicuously lacks.

clue.text: (& 13dn.) Short-arsed PC wants confrontation with old copper, after (straight up)

indicators.note: the confrontation and copper come after the straight-up word

parts.note: standing straight up is vertical, so vertically
a challenge is a confrontation
d was the abbreviation for the old penny, a copper coin

explanation.surface: A short policeman wants a punch-up with a veteran officer.
explanation.walkthrough: PC looks like a police constable, but it means politically correct: the euphemism for short.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertically challenged is the jokey politically correct euphemism for a short person.

clue.text: Masseurs and their safe sex aids abroad?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: people who rub clients' bodies
second meaning: in American English ... are condoms

explanation.surface: Massage parlour staff supplying condoms overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' signals the American usage; British rubbers are erasers.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber is anyone who rubs, such as a masseur, and is also the US slang for a condom.

clue.text: Drink makes one unerotic

indicators.note: the letters make up a new word when rearranged

parts.note: a means one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A claim that alcohol kills the libido.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange-flavoured liqueur, a drink served neat or in cocktails.

clue.text: Wow, love to get hard and rough up …

parts.note: love means zero in tennis, which looks like O

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the hooligan word is written bottom to top

parts.note: a rough is a hooligan, and so is a yob

explanation.surface: An excited exclamation at a lover's erection and some rough play.
explanation.definitionFit: Oh boy is an exclamation of surprise or excitement, like wow.

clue.text: … member of punk group (live appearance in 'Alien')

indicators.note: the live letter appears inside the alien word

parts.note: an alien is a stranger or foreigner
L marks the live wire on a British plug

explanation.surface: A punk band member appears live, maybe in the film Alien.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stranglers were a British punk band of the late 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: A Strangler is a member of the punk rock band the Stranglers.

clue.text: Particular women, in a sexual sense, give alternative head

indicators.note: the word's first letter is swapped for a different one, giving it a new head

parts.note: a vulgar slang term for women regarded sexually

explanation.surface: Reads like a coarse remark about choosy women and oral sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a sexual pun, but it only means the first letter, which changes to F.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone particular is hard to please and exacting, which is what fussy means.

clue.text: Honoured to get oats, maybe, gobbling model

indicators.note: the feed swallows the model letter

parts.note: oats are an example of animal feed
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: An honoured guest gets porridge oats while wolfing down a supermodel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get oats' suggests sex, but oats are just horse feed.
explanation.definitionFit: To fete someone is to honour or celebrate them publicly.

clue.text: Don't be fiddling with stiff 'un!

indicators.note: messing about with those letters rearranges them

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning against masturbating, or meddling with a corpse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't be' is the definition: to cease to exist, that is, die.
explanation.definitionFit: To snuff it is British slang for dying, so no longer being alive.

clue.text: Blair finally gets round House: "May I have your attention …"

parts.note: Blair stands for his first name Tony, whose last letter is Y
round looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Tony Blair at last circles the Commons and calls for quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking Blair as Tony gives the final letter Y, not R.
explanation.definitionFit: Yo-ho is an old interjection used to call for attention, like hey there.

clue.text: Go on, Tony's No. 1 ousted the spiritual leader?

indicators.note: the letter is thrown out of the chattering word, as a leader is ousted from office

parts.note: to rabbit on is British slang for chattering endlessly, so rabbit means go on

indicators.note: Tony's number one is the name's first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Political chatter: Tony Blair's number one has ousted a spiritual leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tony's No. 1' sounds like Blair's deputy, but it is just his initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is the religious teacher and leader of a Jewish congregation.

clue.text: Verity, quite devoid of spin but rather pissed

indicators.note: British slang for drunk, so these letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Verity, refreshingly free of political spin, but somewhat drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Verity' looks like a woman's name, but here it is simply the noun meaning truth.
explanation.definitionFit: Unvarnished truth with no spin on it is the plain, stripped-down fact of the matter.

clue.text: Popular record once, gutless Tony long held to be without any talent

parts.note: in fashion, so in
an extended-play record, a format popular in the past

indicators.note: the long abbreviation is held inside the shortened name
Tony with its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: taken as written
L is an abbreviation for long, as in longitude

explanation.surface: A sneer that the old hit records of a long-famous Tony prove he never had talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something ineptly means doing it clumsily, with no skill or competence at all.

clue.text: Go topless after theatre, as dozy types do

indicators.note: the topless word is placed after the theatre word, so it comes second

parts.note: No is a variant spelling of Noh, the classical Japanese theatre
to doff is to take off clothing, as one does to go topless

explanation.surface: A night out ending with someone stripping off their top after the show.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer comes after the theatre word in the grid, as 'after' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Drowsy, sleepy people tend to drift into a brief sleep, which is nodding off.

clue.text: see 1dn
Ulster Unionist drops extreme characters — the way to achieve Church union?

definitions.text: the way to achieve Church union?

indicators.note: the name loses its letters at both extremes, the first and the last

parts.note: Ian Paisley, the hardline Northern Irish unionist leader

explanation.surface: An Ulster unionist rejecting extremists to bring about the reunion of the churches.
explanation.walkthrough: Church union is a wedding, not ecumenism: the couple walk down the passage between the pews.
explanation.definitionFit: The bride walks up the central passage between the pews to be married, so it is the route to a church wedding.

clue.text: Iain Duncan Smith has one testicle (left out on date) repair

indicators.note: the left abbreviation is taken out of the testicle word

parts.note: ball is slang for one testicle
to patch something is to repair it

explanation.surface: A schoolboy smear on the then Tory leader, plus a date and some mending.
explanation.walkthrough: Iain Duncan Smith, Conservative leader in 2003, is famously bald; 'on' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairless area on the crown is what a balding man such as the then Tory leader has.

clue.text: Bollocks to Frenchmen — they can be so desperate to mate

definitions.text: they can be so desperate to mate

parts.note: bull is slang for nonsense, as is bollocks
Frogs is offensive British slang for the French

explanation.surface: A dismissive retort to Frenchmen who are always desperate for sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Male bullfrogs croak loudly in the breeding season to attract a mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullfrogs are large frogs whose males call loudly and persistently when breeding.

clue.text: No! Paisley has new scheme for these islands!

indicators.note: a new scheme is a fresh arrangement of the letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ian Paisley shouting no at a new plan for Northern Ireland and Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'These islands' suggests Britain and Ireland, but they are in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: Polynesia is the large group of Pacific island groups including Hawaii, Samoa and Tonga.

clue.text: Teaser displaying member — sort who gets the women?

parts.note: a leg is a limb, or member, of the body
a puller is British slang for someone who often attracts sexual partners

explanation.surface: A flasher exposing himself, as if that were how to attract women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' wants to be the obvious rude thing, but it is merely a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pulls your leg is joking or kidding, which is what a teaser does.

clue.text: George, putting on a dress, minced and squealed

indicators.note: minced means chopped up, so the letters are cut and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Boy George in a frock, mincing about and shrieking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minced' and 'squealed' read as camp behaviour; squealed is slang for informed.
explanation.definitionFit: To grass is British slang for informing on someone to the police, as is to squeal.

clue.text: See the state of boozer

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
Cal is an abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: Look how drunk that heavy drinker is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' looks like a drunk, but in British slang it is a pub; a local is one's neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Britons call their nearest regular pub their local, and boozer is slang for a pub.

clue.text: 'Pussy-tramp' is often beneath a model

parts.note: a pussy is a cat
a tramp is a long walk

explanation.surface: Implies that some promiscuous woman often lies under a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' is not a loose woman but a trudge on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashion models parade along the raised runway, so it is literally under their feet.

clue.text: Screw Dicky's reward!

parts.note: screw is British slang for wages, which is pay
dicky is British slang for faulty or unwell, the same as off

explanation.surface: An exclamation that sex is someone named Dicky's prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screw' and 'Dicky' both look sexual; they are slang for wages and for poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: A payoff is a payment or bonus given as a return for something, so a reward.

clue.text: Right off dog's balls

indicators.note: the right letter comes off the dog's name

parts.note: Rover is a stock name for a dog

explanation.surface: A crude remark about removing a dog's testicles.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket overs are made up of balls bowled, so the word stands loosely for deliveries.

clue.text: Pat, deprived of a pee during misguided enema, is a cow mainly

indicators.note: the shortened name sits within the jumbled letters
the enema's letters are sent the wrong way, into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the name loses that letter

parts.note: taken as written
a P, the letter's name spelt out

explanation.surface: A lavatorial tale of Pat, unable to pee during a botched enema, called a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mainly' means in the main, the sea: this is a sea cow.
explanation.definitionFit: The manatee is a large aquatic herbivore known as the sea cow, living in the main or ocean.

clue.text: Married? Doubtful — too quick to take offence

parts.note: iffy is informal for doubtful or uncertain

explanation.surface: A dubious marriage to someone who is touchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Miffy is a colloquial adjective for someone easily annoyed or touchy.

clue.text: Agitation can

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a commotion or excitement
second meaning: ... and can are both slang for prison

explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb or a tin, but both slang senses mean jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A stir is a fuss or commotion, and stir is also old slang for a prison, like the can.

clue.text: Was a wanker executed so casually?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to toss off is vulgar slang for masturbating
second meaning: produced quickly and carelessly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Executed' suggests a hanging, but it only means done or produced.
explanation.definitionFit: Tossed off covers both crude self-gratification and writing or doing something quickly without effort.

clue.text: Western women, including 'name', done over in informal speech

indicators.note: the whole is turned over, so it reads backwards
the women word takes in the abbreviation

parts.note: gals is the American, cowboy-film word for women

explanation.surface: Cowgirls, being named, then beaten up, all described in casual chat.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is the informal vocabulary of everyday speech, as opposed to standard language.

clue.text: Newly-weds eschewing second-class shags

indicators.note: the brides avoid the second-class letter, which drops out

parts.note: brides are women newly married
B denotes the second grade or class

explanation.surface: Newlyweds refusing sex that is second-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shags' could be the seabirds, but here it is the crude verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride is a crude slang term for having sex with someone, the same as shag.

clue.text: Broadcaster given the bird and pissed around?

parts.note: Sky is the British satellite television broadcaster
the lark is a songbird
given is a past participle, taken here for the verb ending that makes the past tense

explanation.surface: A TV presenter booed off and then fooling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given the bird' means booed off, but the bird is a lark; pissed around is British slang for messing about.
explanation.definitionFit: To skylark is to play about boisterously, the same as fooling or messing around.
